chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you pass by the valley of Muhassar, and it is a great valley between Jam' and Mina, and it is nearer to Mina, so walk briskly in it until you cross it, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) stirred his she-camel and said: 'O Allah, secure my Covenant for me, and accept my repentance, and answer my supplication, and be in my place among those I left behind.'

key_terms.جَمْعٍ: Jam', a place near Mina where pilgrims gather
key_terms.فَاسْعَ: So walk briskly, referring to the specific mode of walking recommended in this valley
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a plain near Mecca used during Hajj
key_terms.وَادِي مُحَسِّرٍ: Valley of Muhassar, a specific location between Jam' and Mina in Mecca

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of walking briskly in the Valley of Muhassar and what supplication did the Prophet recite there?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the Sunnah of brisk walking in the Valley of Muhassar, located between Jamm and Mina, a practice rooted in the Prophet Muhammad’s (peace be upon him and his family) specific supplication for the acceptance of his covenant and legacy. In Shia scholarly tradition, this act is viewed not merely as a physical ritual but as a spiritual purification, connecting the pilgrim to the Prophet’s personal experience and reinforcing the continuity of divine guidance through his Ahl al-Bayt. The supplication emphasizes the preservation of the Prophet’s mission, which Shia theology interprets as extending through the Imams, thereby linking the Hajj ritual to the broader concept of Wilayah.
